draft.title: Unsaved recovery draft found
draft.description: This is the latest valid recovery draft from the current project session. The block comparison below explains what changed. It will not be treated as a saved version or overwrite the project automatically, and older drafts will not keep appearing in this session.
draft.compareAria: Compare recovery draft blocks with current project
draft.compareParseError: The block difference summary could not be parsed: {{error}}. Both previews will still try to render, and the original recovery data will not be changed.
draft.safetyNote: Overwrite current workspace creates a formal checkpoint first and keeps this draft until the project is saved successfully. Restore as new creates another project without changing the original. Keep for later suppresses older drafts from the same baseline for this session; CK will evaluate them again when the project is reopened. If the draft contains third-party blocks that are not installed, CK stops the restore and preserves the original data.

lastWorking.title: Last Working Version
lastWorking.description: Updated only after a normal firmware upload succeeds and passes artifact validation. Debug and trace firmware never overwrite it.

confirm.projectMessage: CK creates a Before Restore checkpoint first, then restores the blocks, generated source, board, and complete configuration. Firmware is not uploaded.
confirm.firmwareMessage: The current project remains unchanged. CK revalidates the chip family, physical Flash, complete FQBN, partition addresses, artifact manifest, and SHA-256 for every segment before writing to {{port}}.
confirm.completeTitle: Restore the complete Last Working Version?
confirm.completeMessage: CK protects the current project first, restores the CK-managed dependency snapshots (backing up replaced versions), then restores blocks, source, board settings, and ck.lock. It finally passes hardware and artifact validation again before uploading to {{port}}. A Core mismatch blocks the restore; CK never installs or downgrades a Core silently.
confirm.rebuildTitle: Run a clean rebuild with locked dependencies?
confirm.rebuildMessage: CK validates ck.lock, Core, CLI, toolchain, and every dependency snapshot, then compiles in an isolated build root. It does not read global Arduino libraries or upload to hardware. Any environment or dependency mismatch blocks the rebuild.
confirm.deleteMessage:
This permanently deletes the locally stored version, dependency snapshots, and firmware copies for the current project.

It does not change the current project, generated source, or firmware already on the board. CK creates a new version after the next normal upload succeeds and passes validation.

lastWorking.deleteTooltip: Delete only the locally stored version; do not change the current project or board firmware
lastWorking.loading: Validating the local Last Working Version…
lastWorking.emptyDescription: After the next successful normal upload, CK stores the complete project, ck.lock, build identity, hardware evidence, and every flashed segment.
lastWorking.compareDescription: Compare blocks, source, Core, complete FQBN, dependencies, configuration, hardware, and resources—not just file hashes.

lastWorking.safetyNote: Firmware restore never bypasses safety checks. CK must revalidate the hardware chip family, physical Flash, partition addresses, complete artifact manifest, and SHA-256. ck.lock remains local and is never uploaded automatically.

checkpoint.title: Project checkpoints
checkpoint.description: Save at any time; CK also protects the project before builds, uploads, and restores
checkpoint.retention: CK keeps the {{count}} most recent checkpoints. Manual and automatic checkpoints use the official project serialization and include variables, procedures, third-party block state, and breakpoints. CK protects the current state again before a restore.
checkpoint.createTooltip: Save the current blocks, source, board, and complete configuration now
checkpoint.desktopOnly: Project checkpoints are available only in the CK desktop app. Web previews never write recovery data.
checkpoint.emptyDescription: Select Save current state, or wait for CK to protect the project automatically before the next build or upload.

vault.title: Read-only protection
vault.description: CK did not pass these blocks to Blockly for deserialization and will not allow a normal save to overwrite the original project. Original fields, connections, coordinates, mutation, extraState, and nested data remain byte-for-byte intact.
vault.openPackages: Install or enable matching block packages
